question_stem:
Fig. 2.1 shows a square metal sheet of non-uniform density, with a thin wooden rod fixed at its centre. One of the corners of the sheet is labelled X.

{{figure:figure_2_1}}

Fig. 2.1

The rod has negligible mass. The mass of the metal sheet is $2.8\text{ kg}$. The rod is supported so that the rod is horizontal and the metal sheet is vertical.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Define the torque of a couple.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
When the rod is supported in such a way that it can rotate freely within its support, the sheet hangs in equilibrium with point X vertically above the rod, as shown in Fig. 2.2.

{{figure:figure_2_2}}

Fig. 2.2

On Fig. 2.2, draw a line to indicate the range of possible positions for the centre of gravity of the metal sheet.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Explain whether the torque applied to the rod to hold the sheet in equilibrium is clockwise or anticlockwise.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Show that the centre of gravity of the sheet has a horizontal displacement of $0.12\text{ m}$ from the rod.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
The square metal sheet has an average density of $3000\text{ kg m}^{-3}$ and a uniform thickness of $4.0\text{ mm}$.

Show that the side length of the sheet is $0.48\text{ m}$.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text: Use the answer in (b) and the information in (c) and (d) to determine the position of the centre of gravity of the sheet. Indicate this position on Fig. 2.3 with a point labelled Y.
